subject.title: fix(memory-core): clear daily-ingestion sqlite namespace on dreaming repair

question: Should `openclaw memory status --fix` clear the persisted `dreaming-daily-ingestion` SQLite namespace whenever it archives the derived dreaming session corpus or legacy session-ingestion artifact?
rationale: This is a small and well-proven bug fix, but it intentionally deletes persisted memory-core bookkeeping and causes daily files to be re-ingested, so the final upgrade/session-state policy belongs to maintainers.

options.title: Land the symmetry fix
options.body: Accept the PR because repair should reset all three ingestion namespaces that audit treats as one derived ingestion state.

options.title: Keep daily ingestion state
options.body: Reject or revise the PR if maintainers want daily-ingestion bookkeeping to survive session-corpus repair despite the audit reporting it as ingestion state.

options.title: Add a narrower repair mode
options.body: Request a separate explicit daily-ingestion reset path if clearing daily state under the existing --fix flow is too broad.

recommendation.title: Land the symmetry fix
recommendation.body: Accept the PR because repair should reset all three ingestion namespaces that audit treats as one derived ingestion state.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged audit-side SQLite fallback that created the symmetry requirement this PR addresses.
